name: Autopilot Watch
tagline: The system watches, measures and tells you exactly what to fix. It changes nothing.
priceNote: per site, per month. No contract.
bestFor: Teams with their own developers who want the diagnosis and the priority order, not the hands.
includes: First full report within five working days of starting
Daily crawl: broken links, redirects, indexability, canonical and robots errors
Core Web Vitals tracked against Google's LCP, INP and CLS thresholds
Structured-data validation on every template
AI-crawler visibility: which answer engines fetched your pages, and which pages
Search Console and GA4 pulled into one weekly report with a ranked fix list
Every finding includes the exact diff needed to fix it
excludes: No changes are made to your site

name: Autopilot Apply
tagline: The safe class of fixes ships unattended. Everything with an opinion in it comes to you as a pull request.
priceNote: per site, per month. Cancel any time; the site stays yours.
bestFor: Owners who want the maintenance burden gone without handing over editorial control.
includes: Everything in Watch
Week one is deliberately visible: speed, broken links and errors fixed first
Unattended fixes for the reversible class: links, sitemaps, image attributes, schema syntax, internal links, performance budgets
Titles, descriptions and content edits proposed as pull requests you approve
Every change is one commit with a stated hypothesis and a one-command rollback
Immutable deploys with instant rollback to any previous build
Public or private changelog of every change made
Kill switch: one command halts all autonomous activity
You keep every change if you cancel — commits in your repo, not an injected script
excludes: No content experiments against a holdout group

name: Autopilot Compound
tagline: Content and conversion experiments, run against a holdout, so the lift is measured rather than claimed.
priceNote: per site, per month. Minimum three months, because the measurement window needs it.
cadence: Daily scan, weekly release, monthly readout
bestFor: Sites where search and conversion are a material revenue line and the gains compound.
includes: Everything in Apply
Page-level holdout: comparable pages are deliberately left alone as a control group
Content rewrites, answer blocks and FAQ expansion aimed at answer-engine citation
Conversion experiments on layout, calls to action and form friction
Monthly readout reporting lift against the control group, including the losses
Query-gap analysis: pages built for demand you rank for but do not serve
Guarantee: if the holdout beats the treatment group two cycles running, that month is free
excludes: Not sold to sites under ~30 comparable pages — a control group needs volume to mean anything
